Sellside Analysts' Memo · Vodafone · built 2 November 2026

How the sell-side sees Vodafone, and where its view is heading

What each broker on record thinks and how that has moved over twelve months, with the Investment Analyst's judgement on where the sell-side goes next.

  • Three kinds of content, each labelled. The brokers' own commentary, from 28 research reports produced between 19 Jun 2026 and 28 Oct 2026 (blue-edged cards). The Investment Analyst's reading of the sell-side, from its Layers 1 to 4 and three memos (purple-edged cards and the judgement boxes). This memo's summaries, tables and charts, which name their sources.
  • Breadth. 1201 passages from 16 research houses, plus consensus and investor views. Every house the research records on this stock is included, however briefly it appears.
  • Checks. Every quotation was matched word for word to its source by script, every summary sentence was checked against the passages, and every number survived the editing.
How current this is, and what was left out

The research reports used here were produced between 19 June and 28 October 2026 and record broker views dated from June 2017 to 27 October 2026, most of them from April to October 2026. The latest dated broker views are Morgan Stanley's and Deutsche Bank's notes of 27 October 2026, and the latest dated rating is Barclays' Sell with a EUR 1.25 target of 19 October 2026 (FactSet). The Investment Analyst's work was written on 27 and 28 October 2026 on FactSet data of 27 October 2026. The next results are the half-year results on 10 November 2026; nothing after 28 October 2026 is covered.

No passage in this set is flagged as stale April to May 2026 research, so none was dropped on that ground. Two passages that stop mid-sentence (Bernstein's VOD1330 and Deutsche Bank's VOD0632) are not used; other cited passages that stop mid-sentence are used only for their complete sentences. Passages about peers only (Tele2, BT, Telia and others) are used only for the read-across the research draws to Vodafone, mainly in the house profiles and the cost-cutting debate.

The answer in brief

  1. Two houses dominate the commentary; FactSet shows a third of brokers at Buy.

    • Deutsche Bank (495 passages) and Morgan Stanley (433) supply most of the commentary among the research passages' sixteen named sources, followed by Bernstein (117), ING's credit research (32), Jefferies (20), Rothschild & Co Redburn (18) and DNB Carnegie (14).
    • The FactSet Buy share was 33% on 27 October 2026; the Investment Analyst's September memo had counted twelve visible brokers on 16 September 2026 (five Buy, five Hold, two Sell).
    • Buy ratings, among eight named in the Investment Analyst's reading of 27 and 28 October 2026: Deutsche Bank (EUR 1.89), Goldman Sachs (EUR 1.80) and Intesa Sanpaolo (EUR 1.59).
    • Hold and Sell ratings in the Investment Analyst's October 2026 reading: Hold at Morgan Stanley (EUR 1.46) and Oddo BHF (EUR 1.17); Sell at Barclays (EUR 1.25), UBS (EUR 1.11) and an unnamed restricted broker (EUR 1.11).
    • Deutsche Bank is the most positive house (Buy, 160p since 30 September 2026); Bernstein was least positive (Underperform, 65p on 11 May 2026) until suspending coverage on 24 July 2026, leaving UBS and the restricted broker with the lowest active targets.
    Source: Research passages (Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, Bernstein); the Investment Analyst's FactSet readings.

  2. Headlines brightened through the year, with Germany the standing caveat.

    • Morgan Stanley's headlines moved over twelve months from "Significant strategic progress, but shares appear fairly valued" (9 January 2026) to "Investment Narrative Shifts; Any Changes Will Take Time" (16 July 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank's long-running Lemony series went from "Lemony twist: Africa boost as Europe recovers. TP u/g. Buy" (22 January 2026) to "Brighter and Less Lemony; TP up; Buy" (30 September 2026); TP is the target price.
    • The May full-year results drew free-cash-flow-beat headlines from both Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank in the last six months.
    • Bernstein's title of 12 May 2026 read "Soft EBITDAaL, weak commercial momentum in Germany, FY27 guidance in-line", before "Full Restriction: Coverage Suspended on VOD.LN" on 24 July 2026.
    • Since late July the titles have been positive on the first quarter, for example Morgan Stanley's "A stronger-than-expected Q1 (Germany, UK, Africa, Group EBITDAaL), guidance raised" (27 July 2026).
    • Since late July the titles have also been positive on the UK, for example Morgan Stanley's "UK Investor Day: Higher Synergy Targets, Very Bullish OpFCF outlook" (8 October 2026); OpFCF is operating free cash flow.
    • The one clearly negative headline of the last three months was Morgan Stanley's "European (ECJ) ruling: Reversing 2023 rise in German fixed price" (14 September 2026); the note said the European Court of Justice ruling would reduce group free cash flow by 1.5%.
    Source: Note titles (Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank, Bernstein).

  3. Targets rose at the two main houses, and FactSet's Buy share rose then slipped.

    • Deutsche Bank kept Buy throughout, moving its target from 140p to 150p (January 2026), to 155p (21 April 2026), back to 150p (15 June 2026, for the delayed buybacks and higher post-merger debt) and up to 160p (30 September 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley kept Equal-weight and moved from 100p to 105p in February 2026 (the passages differ; see conflicts), then raised its target to 115p on 16 July 2026 for higher free cash flow estimates and Vega's 19.9% stake.
    • Morgan Stanley raised its target to 125p on 2 September 2026 for a higher German valuation, and kept 125p after the UK investor day.
    • Bernstein held Underperform with a 65p target (11 May 2026) until it suspended coverage on 24 July 2026; Jefferies' downgrade to Hold, with an 87p downside case, is recorded without a date in a report of 14 July 2026.
    • FactSet's target revisions were +15% over six months, +10% over three months and (2)% over one month to 27 October 2026, when the mean target was EUR 1.45 against a price of EUR 1.42.
    • FactSet's Buy share stood at 33%, up 8 points over six months and 15 points over three months but down 4 points over the last month; the inputs do not name the brokers behind those moves.
    Source: Research passages (Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, Bernstein, Jefferies); note titles; FactSet revisions.

  4. Vega's arrival added a new question: what a new owner will force.

    • The Investment Analyst dates a narrative shift to July 2026, when Xavier Niel's Vega took over e&'s stake and lifted it to 19.9%, adding to the debate over Germany the question of how far a new owner pushes costs.
    • The Investment Analyst describes the narrative as shifting from "self-help that has been paid for" to "what the new owner will force next".
    • Morgan Stanley headlined "New shareholder, new cost targets?" on 2 September 2026 and modelled a doubled net cost target lifting decade-end EBITDAaL by 7% and free cash flow by 26%.
    • Management has not adopted the higher cost target that Morgan Stanley modelled, the research notes.
    • Deutsche Bank called Vega's stake "a vote of confidence in Vodafone's valuation" (30 September 2026); Morgan Stanley had called Niel's 16.2% stake purchase a vote of confidence in portfolio execution (recorded in a report of 14 July 2026).
    Source: Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank research passages; note titles; the Investment Analyst's Layer 1 and memo.

  5. Business arguments (1): Germany is the swing factor, and the court ruling cut estimates there.

    • Germany is the swing factor in most of the research, and Morgan Stanley models German EBITDAaL falling about 2% a year (16 July 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank puts Germany at about 40% of group operating free cash flow (30 September 2026) and sizes the 1&1 wholesale income, which fades as 1&1 builds its own network, at about €400 million a year (21 April 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley cut group free cash flow forecasts by 1.5% after the European Court of Justice ruling against the 2023 price rise, and expected consensus German EBITDAaL declines to worsen from 3% to 4.5% or 5% (14 September 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank modelled the European Court of Justice ruling as a €20 million provision and €10 million a month of lost revenue, but argued that "the German pricing setback is fully manageable" given emerging markets and UK synergies (30 September 2026).
    • Weak German commercial indicators were stressed by both Bernstein (12 May 2026) and ING's credit analyst Jan Frederik Slijkerman (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).
    Source: Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, Bernstein and ING research passages; note titles.

    Germany is the swing factor

    Germany, about 40% of group operating free cash flow, is the swing factor; the European Court of Justice ruling cut Morgan Stanley's group free cash flow forecasts by 1.5%.

  6. Business arguments (2): the UK merger is the agreed offset, and its upgrade was the main positive surprise.

    • VodafoneThree raised its cost synergy target in October 2026 to £1.0 billion a year by financial year 2032, from £700 million by financial year 2030 (Deutsche Bank, 9 October 2026).
    • VodafoneThree set UK operating free cash flow to triple to more than £1.5 billion (Deutsche Bank, 9 October 2026); Morgan Stanley noted the 2032 operating free cash flow target sits about 9% above consensus and 12% above its own estimates (8 October 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank calls the UK synergies "highly bankable", worth about 5% of market value and supportive of its 160p target (30 September 2026).
    • A report of 27 October 2026, citing Deutsche Bank among its sources, concludes that the upgraded target, combined with full ownership of the UK business, "positions the UK as the primary EPS growth engine" (EPS is earnings per share).
    • The caveats are shared: Deutsche Bank expects cash dis-synergies in the first year of integration and intense UK mobile competition (8 and 9 October 2026), and Morgan Stanley expects the merger's network benefits to take three to four years (2 September 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley sees UK mobile service revenue growth plateauing around flat (28 September 2026), and Bernstein argues the £11 billion network commitment is "a reduction in investment rather than a true synergy" (24 September 2026).
    Source: Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley and Bernstein research passages.

  7. Business arguments (3): Africa is the growth engine the main houses credit, and the leakage they measure.

    • Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley agree that consolidating Safaricom adds about €1.1 billion of EBITDAaL in financial year 2027 but brings little immediate cash to the parent (Morgan Stanley, 16 July 2026; Deutsche Bank, 27 July 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank says Africa will be about a third of group EBITDAaL (30 September 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank sees Vodacom's fintech business as undervalued at twice the size of Airtel Money, whose planned London listing at about $7 billion gives a benchmark (23 September 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley stresses "a very large minority interest of 64%" and €300 million to €350 million of extra cash taxes (9 January 2026), and estimates Egypt at about 25% of group operating profit (16 October 2026).
    • The Kenyan court case is the live risk: Deutsche Bank says a failed appeal would remove €1.1 billion of EBITDAaL from financial year 2027 forecasts (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
    • In the Kenyan court case, Morgan Stanley notes Vodacom would still keep a 40% associate stake (29 September 2026).
    Source: Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley research passages.

  8. Estimate revisions were positive over the year, flat over six months and negative in the last month.

    • FactSet's financial year 2027 consensus revisions (27 October 2026), over twelve, six, three and one months: earnings per share +14%, 0%, +10% and (5)%; EBITDA +11%, +1%, +1% and (2)%; sales +5%, 0%, +1% and (3)%.
    • FactSet's mean financial year 2027 earnings per share estimate, also recorded by the Investment Analyst, rose 0.2% over one month, 9.2% over three and 10.9% over twelve, so the two FactSet measures point in different directions over the last month (see conflicts).
    • Consensus earnings per share is EUR 0.107 for financial year 2027 (median; mean EUR 0.113, with brokers ranging from EUR 0.080 to EUR 0.150), EUR 0.130 for financial year 2028 (+21.5%) and EUR 0.142 for financial year 2029.
    • Consensus EBITDA for financial year 2027 is EUR 13,275 million from seven brokers.
    • Morgan Stanley raised its financial year 2027 estimates after the first-quarter results of 27 July 2026, which open the three-month window: free cash flow 6%, EBITDAaL 1.5% and earnings per share about 18% (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
    • The Investment Analyst ties the recent dip mainly to the European Court of Justice ruling, alongside the change at the German fibre joint venture OXG Glasfaser, the Kenyan court case and currency.
    • Morgan Stanley cut its financial year 2027 group EBITDAaL forecast from €13,309 million to €13,253 million after the European Court of Justice ruling (14 September 2026); a research report says this reassessment dragged down FactSet consensus revisions in October 2026.
    Source: FactSet revisions (27 October 2026); the Investment Analyst's consensus table; Morgan Stanley research passages.

  9. On valuation the houses split between a cheap European stub and a fully valued group.

    • Deutsche Bank argues the European business trades at about 3x to 4x EBITDAaL, against a 6.4x peer average, and that a group free cash flow yield above 15% protects the downside (15 June 2026; reports of 14 July to 18 August 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley reaches 125p by sum-of-the-parts with a 6.5% to 8.0% cost of capital for Vodafone Europe (2 September 2026), and applies 5.0x EBITDA to Vodafone Europe in its bear case; Morgan Stanley's scenarios run from 60p to 175p.
    • Morgan Stanley said a 7.0% free cash flow yield "screens at the expensive end of its historical range" (16 July 2026).
    • Bernstein's 65p implied 4.8x EBITDA, and Bernstein called the sector's 16x to 17x forward earnings an unwarranted premium to its ten-year average of 14x to 15x (September 2026).
    • The Investment Analyst records a 24-month forward price-to-earnings ratio of 10.03x on 27 October 2026, the 69th percentile of five years against a median of 9.23x, and puts the Investment Analyst's own fair multiple at about 12x two-year-forward earnings.
    Source: Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley and Bernstein research passages; the Investment Analyst's Layer 1 and memo.

  10. The research sees investors focused on leverage and paused buybacks, under-weighting a German risk and longer-term positives.

    • The sell-side praises the long-term cash flow outlook while investors focus on leverage and the suspended buybacks, the research says, citing Deutsche Bank's briefing of 9 October 2026.
    • A report of 10 August 2026 records that the buyback suspension "disappointed yield-seeking investors", and a report of 10 August 2026 records a positive market reaction to the first-quarter results.
    • Deutsche Bank says the market is "excessively focused on downside risks" (30 September 2026), and the Investment Analyst quotes Deutsche Bank that long-only investors historically "demur on the asset class".
    • Investors have "prematurely dismissed" the risk of a self-reinforcing German decline, a narrative report of 28 October 2026 judges.
    • The 2028 UK pricing step and the Vega cost case are underweight in investor positioning and dialogue, according to the narrative report of 28 October 2026.
    Source: Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley research passages; the research's narrative report; the Investment Analyst's Layer 1.

  11. The Investment Analyst's judgement: the skew in estimates is to the downside over 18 months.

    • The sell-side has moved "from scepticism to cautious acceptance", the Investment Analyst judges, describing "an upgrade cycle that has paused".
    • Consensus will hold financial year 2027 EBITDAaL and cash but cut earnings per share for financial years 2028 and 2029 by 5% to 12% over 18 months, in the Investment Analyst's view, mostly below EBITDAaL (financing, minorities and tax).
    • Net revisions will stay negative through the 10 November 2026 results and the February 2027 trading update, the Investment Analyst expects, turning neutral around May 2027 if a buyback is announced.
    • The mean target at the share price says "the sell-side sees no upside at consensus numbers", in the Investment Analyst's reading, and the Investment Analyst expects ratings to converge on Hold from both sides.
    Source: The Investment Analyst's Layer 1, Layers 3 and 4, and memo.

    The upgrade cycle has paused

    Investment Analyst: consensus will hold financial year 2027 EBITDAaL and cash, but cut financial year 2028 and 2029 earnings per share by 5% to 12% within 18 months.

Where the sell-side's view is heading

The Investment Analyst's judgement

The Investment Analyst judges the upgrade cycle has paused and expects consensus earnings per share for financial years 2028 and 2029 to be cut.

  • Up over the year: FactSet net revisions to financial year 2027 earnings per share were +14% over twelve months, and the mean estimate rose 10.9%; the Investment Analyst reads a move from scepticism to cautious acceptance.
  • Six and three months: net revisions to earnings per share were flat over six months and +10% over three, and to target prices +15% over six months; the Buy share rose 15 points over three months.
  • Turned last month: net revisions to earnings per share were (5)% and the Buy share fell 4 points to 33%; the Investment Analyst calls it a paused upgrade cycle, turned by the European Court of Justice ruling.
  • Where next: the Investment Analyst expects consensus to be held on financial year 2027 EBITDAaL and cash, but cut 5% to 12% on earnings per share for financial years 2028 and 2029 over 18 months.
  • Why: the Investment Analyst calls the +21.5% step in financial year 2028 earnings per share the market's main error: it rests on financing, minority and tax lines carried forward from a flattered financial year 2026 base.
  • When: the Investment Analyst expects the cuts in two steps, the half-year components on 10 November 2026 and guidance for financial year 2028 in May 2027, with ratings converging toward Hold.
  • What would prove it wrong: by the Investment Analyst's own tests, a Vega-related announcement before May 2027, guidance for financial year 2028 above consensus EBITDAaL, or first-half minorities below EUR 250m.

What each broker says

Each research house in turn, ordered by how much the research records from it: its view in one line, then how it frames the case, its arguments, its worries and how its view changed. Quoted words are the research report's.

Deutsche BankRobert Grindle (also John Karidis; Benjamin Yokyong-Zoega on UK consumers)Buy, target 160p (30 Sep 2026); FactSet: Buy, EUR 1.89 (27 Oct 2026)

Deutsche Bank is the most positive voice: Buy throughout, target raised to 160p on 30 September 2026, framing Vodafone as a portfolio with a cheap European stub.

Stance and how it got there

  • Deutsche Bank's Robert Grindle is the most positive voice in the research, at Buy throughout; FactSet records Buy at EUR 1.89.
  • Deutsche Bank's target path: raised from 140p to 150p in January 2026, to 155p on 21 April 2026, trimmed to 150p on 15 June 2026 and raised to 160p on 30 September 2026.
  • Deutsche Bank's June trim followed the agreed £4.3 billion purchase of the 49% UK minority stake, which delayed buybacks and raised debt.
  • Deutsche Bank also cut its financial year 2027 EBITDAaL expectation by 5% in June, and its earnings per share estimate by 24.9%.
  • Deutsche Bank's June title still read One battle after another (but fewer and with peace dividends ahead). Buy.

How it frames the case

  • Deutsche Bank frames Vodafone as a portfolio with a cheap European stub, in which emerging markets, UK synergies and buybacks offset a slow German revival.
  • Deutsche Bank's Grindle called Vodafone a distinctly cheap equity stub opportunity in January 2026, as Vodafone left Italy and Spain.
  • Deutsche Bank says the market values the European business at about 3x to 4x EBITDAaL, against a 6.4x peer average, and cites a group free cash flow yield above 15% (15 June 2026; reports of 14 July to 18 August 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank's forecasts of 30 September 2026: financial year 2027 EBITDAaL of €13.30 billion, at the top of guidance, and 20% growth in adjusted free cash flow in financial year 2027.
  • Deutsche Bank forecast leverage peaking at 2.4x and €2 billion a year of buybacks resuming in financial year 2028 (30 September 2026).

Main arguments

  • Deutsche Bank's main positive arguments are the UK and Africa; Deutsche Bank calls the UK cost synergies highly bankable, worth about 5% of market value (30 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank says the upgraded £1.0 billion target should triple UK operating free cash flow (9 October 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank sees Vodacom's fintech business as twice the size of Airtel Money, whose planned listing gives a valuation benchmark (23 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank treats Vega's 19.9% stake as support for the simplification agenda and argues that the remaining uncertainties are minor and already priced in by the market (30 September 2026).

What worries it

  • Deutsche Bank's worries are specific: Germany is about 40% of group operating free cash flow, and the 1&1 contract is about €400 million of wholesale revenue that fades as 1&1 builds its own network.
  • Deutsche Bank modelled the court-ordered price reversal as a €20 million provision plus €10 million a month of lost revenue (30 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank warns that Africa at a third of EBITDAaL raises currency risk (30 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank warns that a failed Kenyan appeal would remove €1.1 billion of financial year 2027 EBITDAaL (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank warns that UK competitors' tariff cuts could force VodafoneThree to reinvest its savings (8 October 2026).

How its view changed

  • Over twelve months Deutsche Bank's rating has not moved and its confidence has grown.
  • Over six months Deutsche Bank absorbed the buyback suspension and then welcomed Vega.
  • Over the last three months Deutsche Bank raised its target to 160p and, after the UK briefing, titled its 9 October 2026 note calm, clear and confident (execution now key).

Morgan StanleyTerence Tsui, Emmet Kelly, Harrison Williams; Viwe Kupiso on South AfricaEqual-weight, target 125p (2 Sep 2026, kept in a report of 27 Oct 2026); FactSet: Hold, EUR 1.46 (27 Oct 2026)

Morgan Stanley is Equal-weight with a 125p target, framing Vodafone as a cash flow recovery capped by Germany; the Vega cost case is its most distinctive positive argument.

Stance and how it got there

  • Every Morgan Stanley rating recorded in the research, from February to October 2026, is Equal-weight.
  • Morgan Stanley raised its target from 105p to 115p on 16 July 2026, for higher free cash flow estimates and Vega's 19.9% stake.
  • Morgan Stanley raised its target to 125p on 2 September 2026, for a higher German valuation after a resilient first quarter.
  • A report of 27 October 2026 records Morgan Stanley's 125p target kept after the UK investor day.
  • Morgan Stanley framed the shares as fairly valued earlier in the year, under the title Significant strategic progress, but shares appear fairly valued (9 January 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley's July title Investment Narrative Shifts; Any Changes Will Take Time marks a more open view.

How it frames the case

  • Morgan Stanley frames Vodafone as a cash flow recovery capped by Germany, seeing adjusted free cash flow at a turning point, growing about 8% a year over three years (16 July 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley models German EBITDAaL falling about 2% a year and ranks Vodafone last of three German operators on network quality (16 July 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley's sum-of-the-parts suggests limited upside after the first quarter (recorded in a report of 17 September 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley's scenarios run from a 60p bear case (German EBITDAaL deeply negative, 16 July 2026) to a 175p bull case (German turnaround and smooth UK integration, 1 September 2026); options pricing in January 2026 implied an 88p floor.

Main arguments

  • Morgan Stanley's most distinctive positive argument is the Vega cost case: on 2 September 2026 Morgan Stanley argued that the €1.0 billion net cost target removes only 5% of a €19.3 billion European cost base.
  • Doubling the net cost target would lift decade-end EBITDAaL by 7% and free cash flow by 26%, Morgan Stanley argued (2 September 2026); the research notes that management has not adopted the higher target.
  • Morgan Stanley's title after the UK investor day spoke of a Very Bullish OpFCF outlook (operating free cash flow), with the 2032 target about 9% above consensus (8 October 2026).
  • More than 95% of Vodafone's debt is fixed-rate, Morgan Stanley stresses (8 October 2026).

What worries it

  • Morgan Stanley's worries are Germany, the pace of cost cutting and currency; after the European Court of Justice ruling Morgan Stanley cut group free cash flow forecasts by 1.5% (14 September 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley also cut financial year 2027 group EBITDAaL from €13,309 million to €13,253 million after the ruling, and called the price reversal a near 100% margin revenue loss (14 September 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley notes that cost cutting slowed about 45% over four years (2 September 2026).
  • Vodafone faces a very large minority interest of 64% on Safaricom's earnings, Morgan Stanley notes (9 January 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley puts Egypt at about 25% of group operating profit (16 October 2026) and notes that UK mobile service revenue growth has plateaued around flat (28 September 2026).

How its view changed

  • Over twelve months Morgan Stanley moved from a fairly valued view (January and March 2026) to two target raises in July and September 2026.
  • Over the last three months the court ruling pulled Morgan Stanley's estimates down, while the UK investor day and the Vega scenario supplied its most constructive arguments; the rating stayed Equal-weight.
  • Morgan Stanley's financial year 2028 estimates sit about 3% below the average analyst expectation for revenue, EBITDAaL and free cash flow (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).

BernsteinUlrich RatheCoverage suspended (24 Jul 2026); last view Underperform, target 65p (11 May 2026)

Bernstein was the most negative house, at Underperform with a 65p target set on 11 May 2026, and has had no rating since 24 July 2026.

Stance and how it got there

  • Bernstein's Ulrich Rathe was the most negative house: Underperform with a 65p target set on 11 May 2026, 46% below the 120.4p close.
  • Bernstein's stance was anchored on weak German commercial momentum and soft EBITDAaL, and its 12 May 2026 title read Soft EBITDAaL, weak commercial momentum in Germany, FY27 guidance in-line.
  • Bernstein published Full Restriction: Coverage Suspended on VOD.LN on 24 July 2026, because Société Générale and its affiliates were advising Vega on its stake.
  • Bernstein's tone had been less negative in November 2025, when a title read EM continues to power growth as trends in Germany improve and a reduction in capex supports FCF (EM is emerging markets and FCF free cash flow).

How it frames the case

  • Bernstein's case rests on Germany and on cash leakage.
  • Bernstein's 65p downside case implies 4.8x EBITDA, a 5.7% cost of capital for German assets that make up about 45% of enterprise value, and 0.2% terminal growth (recorded in reports of 14 July and 18 August 2026).
  • Bernstein deducts a £4.8 billion spectrum liability, worth about 17p a share (recorded in reports of 14 July and 18 August 2026).

Main arguments

  • Bernstein argues that asset sales were done at unattractive multiples and that disposal proceeds fund temporary buybacks rather than being reinvested to revive organic growth (recorded in a report of 14 July 2026).
  • Bernstein says Vodafone's African stub overstates accessible free cash flow by about €180 million a year (recorded in a report of 18 August 2026).
  • Bernstein noted that the BBB rating sits only two notches above non-investment grade (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
  • The research still records Bernstein notes after the suspension, dated 24 September to 19 October 2026, mostly on the UK and German markets and the sector; these post-suspension attributions are listed under conflicts.
  • Bernstein argues the £11 billion VodafoneThree network commitment, £1.1 billion a year against £1.3 billion before the merger, is a reduction in investment rather than a true synergy (24 September 2026).
  • Discounting by alternative networks may stop VodafoneThree using its pricing freedom after the caps lapse in 2028, Bernstein argues (24 September 2026).
  • A German order to replace Chinese 5G radio equipment could cost Vodafone up to €0.7 billion, Bernstein argues (2 October 2026).

How its view changed

  • Over twelve months Bernstein's titles moved from crediting emerging markets and improving German trends (November 2025) to soft EBITDAaL and weak German momentum (May 2026).
  • Bernstein kept Underperform with a 65p target set on 11 May 2026, before the full-year results, and reported a fourth-quarter EBITDAaL miss of 4.4% against consensus after them.
  • Bernstein has had no rating since 24 July 2026, and the Investment Analyst still uses Bernstein's suspended 65p as the lowest bear anchor among the brokers.

INGJan Frederik Slijkerman (credit research, ING Wholesale Banking)No equity rating recorded (credit research)

ING's coverage is credit research, not an equity rating; its main concerns are leverage and refinancing, and it sees Vodafone's credit profile as weaker than Orange's.

How it frames the case

  • ING's coverage in the research is credit research from ING Wholesale Banking, not an equity rating.
  • ING's credit analyst Jan Frederik Slijkerman called the financial year 2026 performance a solid set of results, with bond spreads at fair value, but said its value depended on improving Germany (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).
  • Deutsche Telekom added 200,000 branded contract mobile customers in Germany in the first quarter of 2026 while Vodafone lost 77,000, ING's Slijkerman noted (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).
  • An ING note title of 28 November 2024 read Vodafone/Same name, different company.

Main arguments

  • ING's positives are Vodafone Greece's proposed fibre joint venture as a deleveraging tool (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026) and falling sector capital spending (21 October 2026).
  • ING still expects Vodafone's absolute capital spending to rise while Vodafone integrates the UK (22 October 2026).

What worries it

  • ING's main concerns are leverage and refinancing: the UK minority buyout adds 0.4x to group leverage, and maturing low-coupon bonds will be refinanced at higher rates (12 May 2026).
  • ING sees downgrade risk if policy ceilings are breached (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • ING sees Vodafone's credit profile as weaker than Orange's (8 November 2024) and, in a report of 27 October 2026, weaker than Telia's and Orange's.

JefferiesJerry Dellis; Martin Comtesse (macro); Akshat AgarwalHold, undated (recorded in a report of 14 Jul 2026); 87p downside case

Jefferies is recorded as having downgraded Vodafone to Hold, with an 87p downside case, and its other recorded views are mostly negative.

Stance and how it got there

  • Jefferies' Jerry Dellis is recorded as having downgraded Vodafone to Hold on persistent margin and pricing pressure, with an 87p downside case under severe cost inflation.
  • The Jefferies downgrade is undated in the report of 14 July 2026 that records it; the only Jefferies downgrade in the note titles is Intractable Headwinds; Downgrade to Hold of 13 May 2022 (see conflicts).

Main arguments

  • Jefferies sees a positive in the transformation, which shifts the group's focus toward high-margin mobile financial services in Africa (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).
  • Jefferies' Martin Comtesse sees public sector demand for information technology services recovering, a positive on the German economy rather than Vodafone itself (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
  • Jefferies' earlier work found a peer operator's cost programmes delivered net savings of about 38% of gross (13 January 2020), which the research uses to call Vodafone's 50% net target ambitious.

What worries it

  • Jefferies' other recorded views are mostly negative: German service revenue faces headwinds from lost collective cable contracts (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Jefferies says the deferred tax asset is overstated in economic value (recorded in a report of 17 September 2026).
  • Elevated spot energy prices could add €400 million a year to costs, in a Jefferies estimate that other passages date to a Jefferies note of 13 May 2022.

Rothschild & Co Redburn has no recorded rating; its work is mostly on peers and costs, and its peer work cuts both ways on the Vega cost case.

Main arguments

  • Redburn called the Italian divestment a bold statement with no sacred cows (recorded in a report of 14 July 2026).
  • Redburn's peer work cuts both ways on the Vega cost case: on 16 July 2026 Redburn argued that Telia and Tele2 expanded service margins by 100 to 150 basis points through cost cutting.
  • Redburn reported in October 2026 that Tele2 is finding it increasingly difficult to deliver further cost savings.

What worries it

  • Redburn flagged €800 million of German revenue at stake from the end of bulk television billing (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
  • Redburn estimated that interest income on disposal proceeds will level off and add to financing costs (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Redburn warned in March 2024 that leverage and African dividend leakage would restrict the scale of buybacks.

Where the brokers disagree

Is the German decline structural, or is the market stabilising?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank says the German broadband market stays disciplined, with little destructive price competition (19 October 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank says the fibre build of the German joint venture OXG Glasfaser, about 100,000 homes a quarter, can stem broadband losses (30 September 2026).
  • Price discipline lifted German fixed service revenue by 0.1% in the fourth quarter, in Deutsche Bank's view as recorded in a report of 27 October 2026.
  • Morgan Stanley's Terence Tsui also sees German mobile competition stabilising, as Telefónica Deutschland launched value-focused bundles with a minimum price point of €30 a month (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley models German EBITDAaL falling about 2% a year and ranks Vodafone's German network last of three (16 July 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley sees the court-ordered price reversal cutting German EBITDAaL by 1.5% in financial years 2027 and 2028 (14 September 2026).
  • Weak German indicators or the need for fibre are stressed by Bernstein (12 May 2026), ING's credit analyst (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026) and Dell'Oro Group (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank itself warns that the 1&1 wholesale benefit laps in financial year 2027 (15 June 2026).

Will the UK synergy upgrade deliver the cash it promises?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank calls the UK cost synergies highly bankable, worth about 5% of market value (30 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank expects UK operating free cash flow to triple to more than £1.5 billion by financial year 2032 (9 October 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley says the 2032 UK operating free cash flow target is about 9% above consensus and that the £11 billion network plan should earn a long-term pricing premium (8 October 2026).

The more negative side

  • Bernstein argues the £1.1 billion a year network commitment is below the £1.3 billion spent before the merger, so the synergy is a cut in investment (24 September 2026).
  • Bernstein argues that discounting may block pricing freedom after the 2028 caps lapse (24 September 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley warns consumer inertia may keep VodafoneThree margins flat (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026), that UK mobile revenue has plateaued (28 September 2026) and that merger access rules could let SpaceX enter (12 October 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank expects cash dis-synergies in the first year of integration (9 October 2026).

Does Africa add value for Vodafone shareholders, or mostly leakage and currency risk?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank says Vodacom's fintech business is twice the size of Airtel Money, whose planned listing at about $7 billion gives a benchmark (23 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank says Safaricom consolidation is cash-flow accretive and adds visibility (30 September 2026).
  • Another passage records a 3.2% cut to Deutsche Bank's adjusted free cash flow forecast, to €2.80 billion, for minority dividend timing, from the earlier consolidation date in the same 30 September 2026 note.
  • Morgan Stanley calls the Safaricom deal strategically positive (28 May 2026), and Jefferies credits the shift toward mobile financial services in Africa (recorded in a report of 27 October 2026).

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley stresses the 64% minority interest and €300 million to €350 million of extra cash taxes (9 January 2026), and Egypt at about 25% of group operating profit (16 October 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank warns a failed Kenyan appeal would remove €1.1 billion of financial year 2027 EBITDAaL (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Bernstein says the African stub overstates accessible cash by about €180 million a year (recorded in a report of 18 August 2026).
  • Emkay, Zedcrest Wealth and IC Securities point to emerging-market discounts, currency losses and Kenyan tax risk.

Is there large upside from cost cuts under Vega?

The more positive side

  • Morgan Stanley says the €1.0 billion net target is only 5% of the European cost base and that doubling it would add 7% to decade-end EBITDAaL and 26% to free cash flow (2 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank sees Vega's 19.9% stake accelerating simplification after 11,000 European roles were cut (30 September 2026).
  • DNB Carnegie says the Tele2 model would enable the largest sector repricing (5 October 2026).
  • Redburn found Telia and Tele2 widened margins by 100 to 150 basis points (16 July 2026).

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley also notes cost cutting slowed about 45% over four years and that Vega's approval may wait until summer 2027, delaying visible cuts to 2028 (2 September 2026).
  • Bernstein says Tele2's growth slowed to 4% as headcount savings ran their course (July 2026), and Redburn reports Tele2 finding further savings increasingly difficult (October 2026).
  • DNB Carnegie finds two of three Telia programmes failed (recorded in a report of 14 July 2026).
  • Jefferies found that a peer operator's net savings ran at about 38% of gross targets (13 January 2020).

Is the stock cheap, or already fairly valued?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank says the market values the European stub at about 3x to 4x EBITDAaL against 6.4x for peers, and cites a free cash flow yield above 15% (June to August 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank says the market is overly focused on downside risks (30 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank (EUR 1.89) and Goldman Sachs (EUR 1.80) hold the highest FactSet targets.

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley found a 7.0% free cash flow yield at the expensive end of the stock's history (16 July 2026) and sees limited sum-of-the-parts upside.
  • Bernstein's 65p implied 4.8x EBITDA.
  • Barclays (EUR 1.25), UBS and a restricted broker (EUR 1.11) rate the shares Sell.
  • The FactSet mean target of EUR 1.45 sat near the EUR 1.42 price on 27 October 2026.

Will buybacks return on schedule without stretching the balance sheet?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank expects leverage to peak at 2.4x in financial year 2027 and fall below 2.25x by financial year 2028, with €2 billion a year of buybacks resuming in financial year 2028 (30 September 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank argues debt capacity could release up to €5.0 billion (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley says more than 95% of the debt is fixed-rate, limiting refinancing risk (8 October 2026).

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley puts leverage after the UK buyout at 2.6x (recorded in a report of 18 August 2026) and warns the £11 billion UK programme could limit buyback cash if Europe weakens (8 October 2026).
  • ING sees higher refinancing costs (12 May 2026) and downgrade risk if leverage ceilings are breached (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  • Bernstein noted the BBB rating is two notches above non-investment grade (recorded in a report of 10 August 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank warns a sudden loss of 1&1 could force a permanent buyback suspension (30 September 2026).

Where the research reports conflict. Both versions are shown; this memo does not pick one.
  1. The July memo's 105p: Morgan Stanley's target or the writer's own estimate?
    • Morgan Stanley's own target, in one place: the Investment Analyst's July memo (price and valuation data of 3 July 2026) records a 105p target as "Morgan Stanley's own standalone price target".
    • The writer's own estimate, elsewhere in the same July memo: the target-price figure is "Watson's own midpoint estimate from the three named broker targets cited in the source report".
    • A research report of 14 July 2026 separately records Morgan Stanley's 105p target with an Equal-weight rating.
  2. Consensus mean target: 154.07p in the research against EUR 1.45 in FactSet.
    • 154.07p in the research: a research report of 17 September 2026 states "The consensus mean target sits at 154.07p", with the lowest targets near 85.59p.
    • EUR 1.45 in FactSet: the Investment Analyst's FactSet reading of 27 October 2026 gives a mean target of EUR 1.45 against a price of EUR 1.42.
    • EUR 1.44 in the September memo: the Investment Analyst's September memo gives a mean of EUR 1.44 and a median of EUR 1.48 against a price of EUR 1.53 (16 September 2026).
    • Not settled: the figures are in different units and are not converted here, and the research does not say which brokers make up the 154.07p mean.
  3. Bernstein views recorded after its coverage was suspended.
    • Coverage suspended: the note titles record "Full Restriction: Coverage Suspended on VOD.LN" on 24 July 2026, and the research records Bernstein's last rating as Underperform with a 65p target (11 May 2026).
    • Bernstein views still appear after the suspension: research passages dated 24 September to 19 October 2026 nevertheless attribute Vodafone-specific statements to Bernstein.
    • Examples of post-suspension Bernstein statements: a German order to replace Chinese 5G radio equipment risks up to €0.7 billion for Vodafone (2 October 2026), and Vodafone's multiple sits at the 47th percentile (29 September 2026).
    • Not settled: some passages call Bernstein's 19 October 2026 item a thematic report or an industry update, and the inputs do not say whether the Vodafone-specific statements came from sector notes.
  4. Two valuation points attributed to both Bernstein and Morgan Stanley.
    • The 47th percentile point, attributed to Bernstein: a research report of 13 October 2026, in one passage, credits a Bernstein note of 29 September 2026 with Vodafone's multiple at the 47th percentile, leaving room to re-rate if cost cuts happen.
    • The 47th percentile point, attributed to Morgan Stanley: another passage of the same research report of 13 October 2026 credits Morgan Stanley with that point.
    • The sector premium view, attributed to Bernstein: one passage credits Bernstein (September 2026) with the view that the sector's 16x to 17x forward earnings is an unwarranted premium to the ten-year average of 14x to 15x.
    • The sector premium view, tagged to Morgan Stanley: another passage tags that view to Morgan Stanley, without the house named in the text (recorded in a report of 28 October 2026).
  5. Morgan Stanley's February 2026 target: 100p or 105p?
    • 100p in February 2026: a report of 27 October 2026 says Morgan Stanley's Terence Tsui "maintained an Equal-weight rating on Vodafone with a price target of 100p in February 2026".
    • 105p from 9 February 2026: a table in a report of 17 September 2026 records a Morgan Stanley raise from 100p to 105p on 9 February 2026, and a report of 14 July 2026 gives 105p.
  6. Deutsche Bank's target in early July: 155p or 150p?
    • 155p in early July: the Investment Analyst's July memo (data of 3 July 2026) describes Deutsche Bank's 155p as "street-high".
    • Cut to 150p on 15 June 2026: research passages record that Deutsche Bank cut its target from 155p to 150p on 15 June 2026.
    • The Investment Analyst's September memo also records the June cut: "Deutsche Bank trimmed 155p to 150p in June 2026 (3 percent) for the buyback delay".
  7. Deutsche Bank's latest target move: date, reason and an undated cut.
    • 160p from 30 September 2026, tied to UK synergies: the note title of that date ("Brighter and Less Lemony; TP up; Buy") records a target increase without a figure, and one passage puts Deutsche Bank's target at 160p from that date.
    • The same Deutsche Bank passage also cites synergies of £1.0 billion by financial year 2032, a target that other passages date to the UK briefing of 8 and 9 October 2026.
    • Other dates and reasons for Deutsche Bank's 160p: another passage reports the 160p target on 9 October 2026, and a report of 27 October 2026 ties the raise to the value of Vodacom's African money business.
    • An undated Deutsche Bank cut: a report of 28 October 2026 separately says Deutsche Bank "adjusted its discounted cash flow target price downward" for a higher share count, without a date.
  8. Did Deutsche Bank upgrade the rating, or only the target?
    • Rating upgrade, in a report of 14 July 2026: the report says "Deutsche Bank upgraded Vodafone", describing the story as distinctly un-Lemony.
    • Buy throughout, in Deutsche Bank's note titles: every Deutsche Bank note title since June 2024 that states a rating says Buy.
    • Deutsche Bank's "Distinctly un-Lemony" note of 14 October 2025 reads "TP u/g. Buy", a target upgrade.
  9. When did Jefferies downgrade to Hold?
    • Undated, in a report of 14 July 2026: the report records that "Jerry Dellis of Jefferies downgraded Vodafone to Hold", with an 87p downside case, but gives no date.
    • 13 May 2022, in the note titles: the only Jefferies downgrade there is "Intractable Headwinds; Downgrade to Hold", and the latest Jefferies note title recorded is of 5 December 2022.
  10. The share of Buy ratings differs by source and date.
    • The Investment Analyst's July memo gives a 42% Buy share and a mix of 42% Overweight, 32% Equal-weight and 26% Underweight (data of 3 July 2026).
    • The Investment Analyst's September memo cites a dashboard Buy share of 22% (16 July 2026), and counted five Buy, five Hold and two Sell among twelve visible brokers on 16 September 2026.
    • The research gives roughly 30% Overweight, 35% Equal-weight and 35% Underweight before the first-quarter results, and Refinitiv's 32%, 37% and 32% (recorded in a report of 17 September 2026).
    • FactSet showed a 33% Buy share on 27 October 2026.
  11. Deutsche Bank's financial year 2027 EBITDAaL forecast: €13.30 billion or €13,412 million?
    • €13.30 billion: Deutsche Bank's note of 30 September 2026 forecasts financial year 2027 EBITDAaL of €13.30 billion, at the top of guidance, and a report of 28 October 2026 repeats that figure.
    • €13,412 million: another passage in a report of 28 October 2026 gives Deutsche Bank's financial year 2027 EBITDAaL as €13,412 million (and €14,014 million for financial year 2028), without a date.
  12. Morgan Stanley's free cash flow growth rate is recorded three ways.
    • 8% a year: Morgan Stanley's note of 16 July 2026 projects adjusted free cash flow growing 8% a year over three years, and a report of 28 October 2026 repeats 8%.
    • 9% a year: a report of 27 October 2026 records Morgan Stanley's free cash flow growth as a 9% compound annual rate over three years.
    • 7% a year: a report of 18 August 2026 records Morgan Stanley's free cash flow as a 7% annual rebound from €2.5 billion to €3.2 billion by financial year 2029.
  13. The Investment Analyst gives two landing points for financial year 2028 consensus earnings per share.
    • EUR 0.115 to 0.123, in the Investment Analyst's Layers 3 and 4: "Expect FY28 EPS consensus to fall toward EUR 0.115 to 0.123 over 18 months".
    • EUR 0.124 to 0.125, in the Investment Analyst's memo: if one of the three below-the-line items goes consensus's way, earnings per share of EUR 0.124 to 0.125 is "the likely landing point of consensus over 18 months".
  14. FactSet's one-month move in financial year 2027 earnings per share: (5)% or +0.2%?
    • (5)% in the FactSet revisions file read on 27 October 2026, which describes its financial year 2027 earnings per share figures (+14%, 0%, +10% and (5)% over twelve, six, three and one months) as percentage changes in the sell-side consensus.
    • A research report records the (5)% as a negative revision, and the Investment Analyst calls the FactSet file's figures net revisions.
    • +0.2% in FactSet's mean estimate: the Investment Analyst separately records FactSet's mean financial year 2027 earnings per share estimate as +0.2% over one month, +9.2% over three months and +10.9% over twelve months.
    • Not settled: the inputs do not reconcile the two measures.
